description.en: Master PyTorch tensors, automatic differentiation, and the nn.Module pattern for building neural networks.
description.ta: PyTorch டென்சர்கள், தானியங்கி வகையீடு, மற்றும் நரம்பியல் நெட்வொர்க்குகளை உருவாக்கும் nn.Module வடிவத்தை கற்றுக்கொள்ளுங்கள்.

story_variants.en:
## Vaathiyaar's Toolbox

Vaathiyaar opens a red toolbox labeled 'PyTorch'. "NumPy gave you arrays. PyTorch gives you tensors — arrays that run on GPUs and compute gradients automatically. This is your essential toolkit."

### Tensors: The Foundation

```python
import torch

# Creating tensors
a = torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])       # from list
b = torch.zeros(3, 4)                     # 3x4 zeros
c = torch.randn(2, 3)                     # random normal
d = torch.arange(0, 10, 2)                # [0, 2, 4, 6, 8]

# Operations
result = a * 2 + 1          # element-wise
matmul = c @ c.T             # matrix multiply
reshaped = c.view(6)         # reshape

# GPU support
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    gpu_tensor = a.cuda()    # move to GPU

print(f'Tensor: {a}')
print(f'Shape: {a.shape}, dtype: {a.dtype}')
print(f'Device: {a.device}')
```

### Autograd: Automatic Gradients

```python
x = torch.tensor(3.0, requires_grad=True)
y = x ** 2 + 2 * x + 1  # y = x^2 + 2x + 1
y.backward()              # compute dy/dx
print(f'dy/dx at x=3: {x.grad}')  # 2*3 + 2 = 8
```

### nn.Module: The Building Block

```python
import torch.nn as nn

class MyModel(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, input_dim, output_dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(input_dim, 64)
        self.relu = nn.ReLU()
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(64, output_dim)
    
    def forward(self, x):
        x = self.relu(self.fc1(x))
        return self.fc2(x)

model = MyModel(10, 2)
print(f'Parameters: {sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())}')
```

> **Key Pattern:** Every PyTorch model inherits from nn.Module, defines layers in __init__, and data flow in forward().
story_variants.ta:
## வாத்தியாரின் கருவிப்பெட்டி

வாத்தியார் 'PyTorch' என்ற சிவப்பு கருவிப்பெட்டியைத் திறக்கிறார். "NumPy உங்களுக்கு arrays கொடுத்தது. PyTorch உங்களுக்கு tensors கொடுக்கிறது — GPU-களில் இயங்கி தானாகவே gradients கணக்கிடும் arrays."

explanation.en: Import PyTorch — the deep learning framework
Create a 1D tensor from a Python list. Like numpy array but with GPU and autograd support
Create a 3x4 tensor filled with zeros. Shape: [3, 4]
Random tensor from standard normal distribution. Shape: [2, 3]
Element-wise operations: each element multiplied by 2, then add 1
Matrix multiply: [2,3] @ [3,2] = [2,2]. The .T transposes the tensor
Enable gradient tracking — PyTorch will record all operations on x
All PyTorch models inherit from nn.Module
Define a fully connected layer with input_dim inputs and 64 outputs
Define forward pass — called automatically when you do model(x)
Instantiate model: 10 input features, 2 output classes

executionSteps.explanation: Create tensor from list — like NumPy but with GPU support
Default float dtype is float32 (not float64 like NumPy)
Enable gradient tracking for this tensor
Backward pass: compute dy/dx via chain rule

instruction.en: PyTorch cannot run in this sandbox, so build the same IrisClassifier in numpy, the way nn.Linear, nn.BatchNorm1d and nn.ReLU compute it. Write linear(x, W, b) (x @ W + b), batch_norm(x, gamma, beta) (normalise each feature with the batch mean and variance, eps=1e-5, then scale by gamma and shift by beta), relu(x), forward(X, params) for Linear(4,32) -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> Linear(32,16) -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> Linear(16,3) (dropout does nothing at inference, so it is skipped), and count_params(params) (the total number of numbers in all parameter arrays). For a batch of 10 flowers the output is (10, 3) and the network has 835 parameters.
instruction.ta: இந்த sandbox இல் PyTorch இயங்காது; அதனால் அதே IrisClassifier ஐ numpy இல், nn.Linear, nn.BatchNorm1d, nn.ReLU கணக்கிடும் அதே முறையில் உருவாக்குங்கள். linear(x, W, b) (x @ W + b), batch_norm(x, gamma, beta) (ஒவ்வொரு feature ஐயும் batch சராசரி, variance கொண்டு normalise செய்து, eps=1e-5, பின் gamma ஆல் பெருக்கி beta ஐ கூட்டுங்கள்), relu(x), forward(X, params) — Linear(4,32) -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> Linear(32,16) -> BatchNorm -> ReLU -> Linear(16,3) (inference இல் dropout எதுவும் செய்யாது, அதனால் தவிர்க்கப்படுகிறது), count_params(params) (அனைத்து parameter arrays இலும் உள்ள மொத்த எண்கள்) ஆகியவற்றை எழுதுங்கள். 10 பூக்களின் batch க்கு வெளியீடு (10, 3), network இல் 835 parameters உள்ளன.

practice_challenges.test_code:
import numpy as np
_rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
_x = _rng.standard_normal((6, 5))
_W = _rng.standard_normal((5, 2)); _b = _rng.standard_normal(2)
assert np.allclose(linear(_x, _W, _b), _x @ _W + _b), 'linear must return x @ W + b'
_bn = batch_norm(_x * 3 + 7, np.ones(5), np.zeros(5))
assert np.allclose(_bn.mean(axis=0), 0, atol=1e-6), 'batch_norm must centre each feature (column) on 0'
assert np.allclose(_bn.std(axis=0), 1, atol=1e-3), 'batch_norm must scale each feature to unit variance'
_bn2 = batch_norm(_x, np.full(5, 2.0), np.full(5, 1.0))
assert np.allclose(_bn2.mean(axis=0), 1, atol=1e-6) and np.allclose(_bn2.std(axis=0), 2, atol=1e-3), 'apply gamma (scale) and beta (shift) after normalising'
assert np.array_equal(relu(np.array([-2.0, 0.0, 3.0])), np.array([0.0, 0.0, 3.0])), 'relu must zero the negatives'
_p = make_params(np.random.default_rng(1))
_out = forward(np.random.default_rng(2).standard_normal((10, 4)), _p)
assert getattr(_out, 'shape', None) == (10, 3), 'forward must return one row of 3 class scores per flower'
_h = relu(batch_norm(linear(np.random.default_rng(2).standard_normal((10, 4)), _p['W1'], _p['b1']), _p['g1'], _p['be1']))
_h = relu(batch_norm(linear(_h, _p['W2'], _p['b2']), _p['g2'], _p['be2']))
assert np.allclose(_out, linear(_h, _p['W3'], _p['b3'])), 'forward must apply the layers in the order Linear -> BatchNorm -> ReLU (twice) -> Linear'
assert count_params(_p) == 835, 'count_params must add up the sizes of every parameter array (835 for this network)'

en: batch_norm: mu = x.mean(axis=0), var = x.var(axis=0), x_hat = (x - mu) / np.sqrt(var + eps)

en: Tensors support GPU and automatic differentiation
ta: Tensors முழு எண்களை மட்டுமே வைத்திருக்க முடியும்
Tensors GPU மற்றும் தானியங்கி வகையீட்டை ஆதரிக்கின்றன

q.ta: nn.Module-ல், உங்கள் அடுக்குகளை எங்கே வரையறுக்க வேண்டும்?

under_the_hood.summary: PyTorch combines three mechanisms: tensors that hold data on CPU or GPU, autograd that records operations so gradients can be computed backwards, and nn.Module, which registers the layers and parameters you assign so the whole model can be trained, moved and saved as one object.

steps.title: Tensors: arrays that remember devices
steps.body: torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0, 3.0]) is a float32 array; a * 2 + 1 gives [3, 5, 7] element-wise, and c @ c.T multiplies a (2, 3) tensor by its (3, 2) transpose into (2, 2). The same code runs on a GPU after .to('cuda'), which is the main thing NumPy arrays cannot do.

steps.title: Autograd: requires_grad starts recording
steps.body: For x = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True), y = x² + 3x builds a small graph. y.backward() computes dy/dx = 2x + 3 = 7 and stores it in x.grad. Model parameters have requires_grad=True automatically, so any loss computed from them can be backpropagated.

steps.title: nn.Module registers what you assign
steps.body: When __init__ runs self.fc = nn.Linear(3, 2), Module's __setattr__ records fc as a submodule and its weight and bias as parameters. model.parameters() walks this tree, so the optimizer finds all weights without you listing them; model.to(device) and state_dict() use the same tree.

steps.title: Calling the model runs forward
steps.body: model(x) calls Module.__call__, which runs any registered hooks and then your forward method. Always call the model rather than model.forward(x) directly, so hooks and other bookkeeping are not skipped.

steps.title: Default initialisation
steps.body: nn.Linear(3, 2) does not start at zero. PyTorch fills its weights from a uniform distribution whose range is about plus or minus 1/sqrt(in_features), here about 0.58, and does the same for the bias. Random starting values break the symmetry between neurons so they can learn different features.

props.caption: What a fresh nn.Linear(3, 2) looks like

under_the_hood.takeaway: Tensors carry the numbers, autograd carries the derivatives, and nn.Module carries the structure. Assign layers as attributes in __init__, compute in forward, and PyTorch can find, train, move and save everything for you.
